`Refunder.refund` (`src/refunds.ts`) exists to send a refund back to the card that paid for the original charge, within the shop's refund limits. I read this from the code and from `ostf context src/refunds.ts#Refunder.refund`. I didn't change any files.

**Why it exists**

It implements three requirements:
- **R-REFUND-ORIGINAL** (the `@req` tag on the method): "A refund goes back to the payment method of the charge it refunds, never to another one." It looks up the receipt and calls `gateway.refund(receipt.txn, amount)` on the original transaction.
- **R-REFUND-LIMIT** (declared link): a refund can't exceed what is left of the charge. Refunds above 500.00 per account per UTC day need a second approval. It enforces this through `checkRefundLimit`, and it keeps the per-charge and per-day running totals. It also rolls those totals back if the gateway call fails. This requirement is marked risk-relevant, so ask before changing this code. It controls RISK-REFUND-ABUSE ("a compromised account or a mistaken operator drains funds through refunds").
- **R-AUDIT-MONEY** (declared link): every refund appends an audit entry with the account, action, amount and receipt.

Those requirements refine the needs N-REFUNDS ("refunds quickly without the business losing money to abuse") and N-ACCOUNT-SAFE.

**Tests covering it**

These are all in `src/refunds.test.ts`:
- **`Refunder > refunds to the original transaction`** verifies R-REFUND-ORIGINAL. It is also linked to R-AUDIT-MONEY.
- **`Refunder > totals refunds per account and UTC day`** verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT through `refund` itself.
- **`checkRefundLimit`** verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT for the helper that `refund` calls.

`src/payments.test.ts#Processor > appends an audit entry` also verifies R-AUDIT-MONEY, but it tests the processor, not `refund`.

All of these links are currently `valid` according to OSTF. I haven't run the tests.

I found no test linked to the gateway-failure rollback or the unknown-receipt error. That isn't proof none exists, since I only looked at the links OSTF lists.
